datePolicy: Approximate geological ages, not exact calendar years. The sea-level chronology is a rounded regional account; the 2013 paper reports radiocarbon ages, not a precise local Kobe shoreline reconstruction. Uplift was gradual, not a single earthquake. Present terrain remains the background.

sources.supports: Rokko granite about 70 Ma; Kobe Group 37–31 Ma; glossary.
Appendix A.1: basin subsidence from about 3.5 Ma; fault activity; Rokko uplift from about 1 Ma.
Rokko uplift and basin subsidence; granite fracture and weathering.
Last-glacial dry land and subsequent marine transgression.
Masuda & Itomoto, 2013: marine entry approximately 9,850 BP; highstand about 6,000 BP.

notes: Ongoing sediment transport and valley/coast shaping are a plain-language synthesis of weathering, streams and basin sedimentation. These processes overlap in time.
